fun_highlights: The vocation system genuinely works: a soldier's life plays structurally different from a scholar's. The vx_ cross-cards (soldier x war era, scholar x turning era, maker x plenty era) are the game's best moments — rare, earned, and surprising.

Callback chains create real emotional payoff. The 'looked away as a child / sees the rough sleeper as an adult / looks away again / or finally stops' arc is one of the finest things a text life-sim can do. When it fires, it earns its place.

The solitary and childless life-shapes are genuine content, not dead-ends. m_solitary, a_chosen_family, e_solitary give a non-domestic life its own texture. That collateral succession doesn't end the house is the right design call.

The dynasty layer adds real cross-life stakes. Watching a house climb from 'a rented room' to 'a house written into the histories' over five generations (House Quint) is genuinely satisfying. The motto crystallisation feels earned.

Prose variety within repeated cards is excellent. The seven variants of y_love1, the age-aware marriage lines, the late-birth pool — these prevent sentence-level repetition. freshPick with global dedup is doing real work.

Era system changes the world's texture generation to generation. A war-era childhood reads differently from a plague-era one. The six era types and their gated cards are light but effective macro-variety.
The 'competing goods' cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_dream_or_duty, x_loyalty_truth) are the genre at its best — no clean answer, both roads carry weight.
staleness: The structural skeleton repeats too visibly by dynasty 5–6. Every life: c_origin → childhood scatter → y_calling → love card → marry → child → midlife health/work → elder legacy → die. This is the exact 'same template with new names' the brief asks about. The vocation arc adds a layer but not enough to disguise the scaffold. By dynasty 8 I was predicting the shape before reading the text.

The calling card (y_calling) fires with near-certainty in every life, and its four choices (blade/book/hands/road) are the only structural fork. Every life ends up in one of four vocation channels. With 15+ dynasties all four channels exhaust themselves: by dynasty 10 I had seen every vocation arc multiple times, and the once-per-dynasty guard on vocation arc cards (a_soldier_service, a_scholar_question, a_maker_shop, a_wanderer_settle) means late-dynasty lives in a given vocation hit the same 3-card arc every time.

High repeat rate on certain universal beats. In the 15-dynasty transcript: cb_lookaway (looked away / rough sleeper callback) fires in dynasties 1, 2, 9, 10, 13, 14 — six times. The m_health 'body sends its first real letter' fires in nearly every life with moderate vit. The u_windfall / u_loss cards recycle constantly in the adult years. These are cooldown-gated, not once-per-dynasty, so they reappear every 14-16 years of game time, which means once per generation reliably.

The adult/midlife band (roughly ages 28–64) is the thinnest. The work promotion card (a_work) fires repeatedly on the same 2-choice structure. The wealth cards (a_fork_career, m_money, m_invest_name) feel like the same decision rephrased. Despite the anti-staleness passes, most adult lives still hit: love → marry → child → work promotion → health scare → aging parent. The variety cards (a_small_lie, a_neighbour, a_belief, a_fallow, m_rival) are low-weight fillers and often cluster in the same sequence.

Epitaph clustering is still noticeable. 'Taught what she knew, and so outlived the knowing of it' appears for Tamsin (D2), Cleo (D4), Anouk (D6), Greta (D5), Lazlo (D7), Annika (D12) — six times in 15 dynasties despite the freshPick dedup. The dedup operates per-session but with a 110-line window; at dynasty 10+ the window has cycled and lines recur. The epitaph pool is genuinely smaller than the play variety suggests.

The dynasty mechanics lack legible negative arcs. A house falls to 'nothing but a name' several times but there are no materially different cards for a FALLEN house vs. a rising one. The repute-gated and seat-gated cards (r_scholar_door, s_great_burden, s_patronage) only fire for high-seat houses. A house in decline never faces structurally different content from a house at seat 1 — it's just the same cards with different seat-based opening text.

improvements.what: Add 2–3 'alternative calling' cards for adult lives with no vocation — a 'late calling' card (age 30–45) that gates a distinct mid-career cluster, parallel to y_calling. This would let a life that missed the youth fork still diverge structurally, and give the adult band a second major fork.
improvements.why: Right now a life that somehow slips the y_calling draw (or dies young) and one that took 'the road' as a teenager both end up in a formless adult band. A second structural fork in the 30s would break the template.

improvements.what: Mark cb_lookaway and m_health as onceDyn (once per dynasty), not once-per-life with a cooldown. They currently fire in nearly every generation of a long house. Once per dynasty is enough for each to feel special.
improvements.why: In the transcript cb_lookaway fires 6 times across 15 dynasties. This is the most visible single source of the 'same beat again' feeling.

improvements.what: Add a low-seat content track: 2–4 cards gated on seat <= 1 that paint a world of genuine scarcity and social invisibility. These should unlock situations inaccessible to wealthy houses (c_steal already does this at age 6, but nothing comparable exists for adult/midlife). Low houses would then feel structurally different from high ones in both directions, not just in the opening text.
improvements.why: Right now a seat-0 house and a seat-4 house play the same adult cards (minus the seat >= 3 gates). The asymmetry only runs upward. A house that has *fallen* should meet different content from one that was always low.

improvements.what: Expand the epitaph pool for the 'teacher' cluster (currently 6 lines) and the 'kind' cluster (currently 5 lines). These two clusters account for roughly a third of all epitaphs in the transcript. Double each pool, and add a dynasty-offset to the freshPick selection so the same cluster can't land on the same line twice in the same house.
improvements.why: The 110-line RECENT_LINES window resets between dynasties effectively, so epitaph lines recur every 4–6 dynasties. A player reading a long run notices the same final sentence.

improvements.what: Add 1–2 'negative dynasty legacy' cards: content that only appears when a house has DECLINED (seat fell this generation, or facedReckoning==='fell'). For example, a card that acknowledges shame, a reputational scar, or a specific hardship the falling house must navigate. This makes the downward arc as content-rich as the upward one.
improvements.why: The current dynasty layer rewards building and is nearly silent on decline. A house that slips from seat 4 to seat 2 faces no new content — the player just sees the standing readout change. Loss should have texture.

improvements.what: Reduce the y_calling draw probability from 0.5 (and near-certain at window end) to something that lets ~15% of lives genuinely miss the fork — and write a small 'drifted life' arc (2–3 cards) for uncalled lives that gives them their own identity rather than playing as structurally undefined adults.
improvements.why: The near-certainty of the calling draw means the four vocation channels exhaust rapidly in a long run. Rare uncalled lives would add structural variety without breaking the dominant pattern.

verdict: A Life has genuine craft and some excellent moments — the callback arcs, the vocation x era intersections, the competing-goods cards — but by dynasty 6 the structural skeleton (origin → calling → love → marry → child → midlife → elder → die) is predictable enough that a genre veteran is anticipating beats rather than discovering them, and the card pool's repeat rate across a 15-dynasty run exposes the seams the prose is working hard to hide.
